source: Stolt Ludwigshafen (BASF, 135 x 17.5 m): about 800 t at Kaub 30 cm, 2,300 t at 100 cm, 5,100 t at full draught (BASF press release 2023); nine such tankers in service in August 2026 (WirtschaftsWoche 18 Aug 2026); Kaub 5-6 cm on 14-17 Aug 2026 (PEGELONLINE)
measures: the payload of one purpose-built tanker at 30 cm (liquid bulk, upstream), and the count of such vessels; no tonnage count exists at 5 cm
transformation: the weekly tonnage of the low-water tankers as a share of the normal Kaub tonnage: nine vessels of 800 t at about two trips a week give 1-2 % of 1 Mt; rounded up to 0.05 for the small dry-cargo units still moving; held at 0.05 below 5 cm

source: press on 14 Aug 2026: shipping past Kaub stopped (Verkehrsrundschau); Contargo and CMA CGM: no container barge below 24 cm (surcharge notices, Aug 2026)
measures: qualitative statements on the Middle Rhine, all cargo
transformation: interpolated between the 5 and 15 cm rows; the statements bound the value above zero and below the 15 cm count

source: KBN (Koninklijke Binnenvaart Nederland) via Schuttevaer, 14 Aug 2026: 60 kt dry and 30 kt wet in the week to about 13 Aug 2026 against a normal 300 and 100 kt
measures: weekly tonnage of the association's members past the Middle Rhine, dry and liquid, both directions, in a week whose daily gauge fell from 23 to 6 cm (mean about 12 cm); denominator the association's own normal week
transformation: the count gives 0.22 of normal at a mean gauge of about 12 cm, the table takes 0.12 at 15 cm: the table sits below the only count at the lowest gauges (an earlier version placed this count at the 25 cm row); the band of the loading table (shortfall x 0.85) reaches 0.14 here, not 0.22

source: Argus Media, Aug 2026: a 1,200 t tanker loads 180 t at 23 cm; the low-water tankers 700-800 t of 5,100 t (BASF 2023, WirtschaftsWoche 2026)
measures: single-vessel payloads, liquid bulk, Kaub 23-30 cm
transformation: vessel share 0.15 times a redeployment of about 1.5 (more vessels for the same cargo) gives the fleet value; the 2026 KBN count (0.22 at about 12 cm) is no longer attributed to this row

source: Kiel Institute statement of 28 Jul 2026 (press): loads 10-15 % of capacity; van Dorsser et al. (2020): at the 2018 record of 25 cm only CEMT class II-III vessels sailed
measures: single-vessel loads at about 30 cm, all cargo; the classes able to sail in 2018
transformation: vessel share about 0.12 times a redeployment of 2 gives the fleet value

source: WSV loading convention: at 40-50 cm a standard vessel carries about 20 %; Contargo surcharge notice, Aug 2026: at 40 cm freight navigation practically impossible for large container vessels
measures: single-vessel load factor of a standard unit (GMS) and the container operator's threshold
transformation: vessel share 0.16-0.20 times a redeployment of 1.5-2 gives the fleet value

source: Contargo surcharge table, 9 Aug 2026: at 55 cm a large container vessel loads 16 %; Schiffahrts-Zeitung / SMC 2026: twice the number of vessels deployed for the same cargo at moderate low water
measures: single large container vessel at 55 cm; the fleet redeployment factor
transformation: 0.16 times a redeployment of 2-2.5 gives the fleet value

source: GlW convention (equivalent low water, 78 cm): Contargo loads 25 % per vessel, four times the ships; Ademmer et al. (2023): a full month below 78 cm lowers German inland-waterway tonnage by about 25 % (monthly, national, all cargo, 1991-2019)
measures: the national monthly tonnage response to a month of low water, and the vessel load at the convention gauge
transformation: the national -25 % for a month below 78 cm, in which Kaub usually sits far below 78, bounds the fleet value from below; the vessel load 0.35 from above

source: Maersk low-water surcharge of EUR 100 per 20-foot container below 91 cm (surcharge notice)
measures: the gauge at which the mild surcharge band starts, containers

source: Kaub 120-125 cm in late April 2026: normal loading reported (press)
full loading of a standard vessel needs about 150 cm at Kaub (hydrostatus, Kiel Institute); the fleet's slack absorbs the residual
transformation: full loading of the fleet from 150 cm

source: Contargo 2017: 250 cm = 100 % for the largest vessels
